subject: SEM model unable to converge when socioeconomic variables included

messages.author: f2309ec8f6aff66b
messages.subject: SEM model unable to converge when socioeconomic variables included
parts:
I'm trying to fit a sem model and include socioeconomic factors (income, educational attainment). I've tried including these variables in a latent variable 'ses' as well as using them as exogenous variables in the regression model. In both cases, the model produces the following warning: 

Warning message:
In pc_cor_TS(fit.y1 = UNI[[i]], fit.y2 = UNI[[j]], method = optim.method,  :
  no convergence

The sample size is n=36015. When I remove all of the socioeconomic factors, the model runs, but adding any one individually to the model produces an error. The simplest model (model 1), without socioeconomic factors, converges and has a good fit. But I want to include these other factors as control variables. Model 3 specifies these factors, and it's the one that don't run. Here's my code:

model1<- "
#Measurement part of model
polpart =~ NA*wrkprty + wrkorg + contplt + sgnptit + pbldmn + bctprd
poltrust =~ NA*trstprl + trstplt + trstprt


#Structural part of model
polpart ~ poltrust + female + agea

polpart~~1*polpart
poltrust~~1*poltrust
"

m1fit<-sem(model=model1, data=ess)



model3<- "
#Measurement part of model
polpart =~ NA*wrkprty + wrkorg + contplt + sgnptit + pbldmn + bctprd
poltrust =~ NA*trstprl + trstplt + trstprt
ses =~ NA*eisced + hinctnta + hincfel


#Structural part of model
polpart ~ poltrust + female + agea + ses

polpart~~1*polpart
poltrust~~1*poltrust
ses~~1*ses
"
m3fit<-sem(model=model3, data=ess)



I'm able to view the model fit using summary(), but the standardized coefficients (std.all) aren't available for model 3. If you have any suggestions for how to make my model converge, please let me know! Thank you :)

messages.subject: Re: SEM model unable to converge when socioeconomic variables included
parts: Standardizing factors, rather than letting a loading be fixed to 1, can make estimates more unstable during minimization. Try allowing the default approach work. You can always standardize results later.

Previously, I had convergence issues with the reduced and full datasets, regardless of the size of the reduced dataset. It's hard to say why it didn't work until I deleted and re-loaded the dataset. No convergence occurred with the full dataset. The second model (factors grouped as latent variable) does not converge with either dataset. Thank you for your assistance!

Kind regards,
Kelly

Error in if (any(abs(rho) > 1)) stop("'rho' must be a valid correlation (-1 <= rho <= 1)") :

I wasn't able to find any documentation on the lavaan website or elsewhere online regarding how to deal with this error message. If you have any advice, please let me know. Thank you for your time!

Kind regards,
Kelly

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: SEM model unable to converge when socioeconomic variables included
parts:
The trust variables 'trstprl', 'trstplt' and 'trstprt' are declared as
'ordered' but they have 11 levels. That leads to numerical issues,
because many pairwise combinations are empty. That is the cause of the
trouble. I have no solution yet (working on it). But I would recommend
to treat these variables as 'numeric'.

(Just out of interest, I tried Mplus on this data. That is how I learned
that Mplus stops with an error if a categorical (endogenous) variable
has more than 10 levels. That makes sense.)

Yves.
